newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan bans Hong Kong visits by soldiers, police.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan bans Hong Kong visits by soldiers, police.

text.p: Taiwan has banned visits by its military and police to Hong Kong now that the territory is part of communist China, Taipei's arch rival, the Central News Agency said on Tuesday.

From July 1, soldiers and police cannot make sightseeing or other pleasure visits to Hong Kong due to security concerns, although exemptions can be made to visit ailing relatives or attend funerals, the state agency quoted officials as saying.
The tightening of rules on visiting the former British colony makes them identical to restrictions that have long applied to visits to the communist mainland itself, it said.
Exemptions to participate in international conferences or business-related activities would be granted on a case-by-case basis, it said.
Taiwan has said the island's extensive civilian contacts and exchanges with Beijing-ruled Hong Kong would remain unchanged.

Beijing, which has seen Taiwan as a renegade province since a 1949 civil war split, maintains that the return of Hong Kong, and Portuguese-run Macau in 1999, will leave Taiwan as the only territory still awaiting "reunification with the motherland".
Taipei officially espouses reunification with the mainland but only when all of China is under a free, democratic system.
